purpose: Separate observed institutional pathways from interpretations and missing causal links.

items.title: Coalition participation to DCLA cultural-plan record

stages.observation: Artists and small cultural-space operators needed routes into a citywide cultural-planning process.
NYC Artist Coalition convened participants, developed priorities, and transmitted recommendations.
CreateNYC records identify the coalition among contributors, and DCLA testimony described work with the coalition.
The official plan records overlapping recommendations; the exact effect of any one coalition contribution on final language remains unresolved.

items.firstMissingLink: A source showing which specific coalition recommendation changed, entered, or strengthened which final plan provision.
nextSources: DCLA drafting or disposition records that map public recommendations to final plan language.
Role-specific accounts from agency and coalition participants.
antiClaims: Do not say the coalition authored CreateNYC.
Do not infer that official inclusion proves every recommendation was adopted.

items.title: Artist experience to Cabaret Law repeal record

stages.observation: Artists and venue operators described the Cabaret Law as discriminatory, burdensome, and disconnected from practical safety.
Jamie and coalition collaborators carried artist experience into public testimony, campaign materials, and safety-policy discussion.
The Council hearing record includes Jamie's testimony and Council engagement with the coalition's perspective.
The Council passed legislation repealing the Cabaret Law.

items.firstMissingLink: A legislative or collaborator record specifying which parts of coalition research or testimony materially shaped bill language, sponsorship, or votes.
nextSources: Council-member and staff accounts of the evidence they found useful.
Bill-drafting history and committee materials connecting issue evidence to legislative choices.
antiClaims: Do not say Jamie or NYC Artist Coalition single-handedly repealed the law.
Do not convert participation in a successful coalition campaign into sole causation.

items.title: Nightlife constituency building to Office of Nightlife

stages.observation: Small venues, artists, and nightlife workers needed a civic interface able to understand cultural and regulatory conditions.
Coalition advocacy and public events helped make small-space and artist concerns visible to officials and the press.
The city created an Office of Nightlife, and coalition town-hall work created an early public feedback surface for its mandate.
The archive does not yet establish which coalition recommendations were adopted in the office's operating model.

items.firstMissingLink: Official formation and implementation records connecting coalition input to the office's mandate, staffing, or early priorities.
nextSources: Council bill, hearing, and sponsor records for the office's creation.
Accounts from Rafael Espinal, Council staff, and early Office of Nightlife personnel.
antiClaims: Do not say Jamie created the Office of Nightlife alone.
Do not imply every town-hall recommendation became agency policy.

items.title: Artist reports to MARCH transparency and oversight

stages.observation: Artists and cultural-space operators reported harmful multi-agency enforcement experiences and insufficient transparency.
The coalition gathered, organized, and amplified reports through public campaign and hearing work.
A Council hearing record identifies coalition research and testimony as part of the oversight record.
The Council enacted reporting requirements; later disbandment of MARCH requires separate official evidence and should not be collapsed into this reporting outcome.

items.firstMissingLink: A complete official chain from coalition findings to reporting requirements and, separately, from oversight to any later operational disbandment.
nextSources: Council committee reports and agency reporting produced under the legislation.
Official records establishing the timing, authority, and rationale of any MARCH disbandment.
antiClaims: Do not say the coalition alone ended MARCH raids.
Do not treat reporting legislation and operational disbandment as the same event.
